title_en: How Much Does It Cost To Charter A Pilatus PC-12 Per Hour In 2026?
title_zh: 2026 年包租一架皮拉图斯 PC-12 每小时要花多少钱？
summary: A PC-12 charters for roughly $2,000 to $3,000 per hour, though positioning flights and fees can move the final figure considerably.
summary_zh: PC-12 的包机费用约为每小时 2,000 至 3,000 美元，但定位航班和费用可能会大幅影响最终数字。
body_en: Brandon's passion for aviation started at a young age. He became involved in the flight simulator and VATSIM communities, which sparked his interest in aviation and eventually led him to earn his private pilot license. Outside of work, he continues to build flight hours, explore new airports, and stay involved in the aviation community.

Chartering a Pilatus PC-12 costs roughly $2,000 to $3,000 per hour in 2026, according to Simple Flying's analysis of private charter pricing drawing on figures from BlackJet and Amalfi Jets. That places the aircraft in the turboprop category alongside the Beechcraft King Air 350i, carrying six to nine passengers on missions up to around 1,500 miles (2,400 km). It is the cheapest way to charter a crewed aircraft of that size.

The hourly rate is also the least reliable number in private aviation. Charter brokers publish PC-12 figures anywhere between $1,000 and $3,500 per hour, and the gap exists because the rate is a starting point rather than a price. Positioning flights to bring the aircraft to the departure airport are billable, which can triple the cost of a short trip. Taxes, fuel surcharges, landing fees, crew overnight expenses and seasonal demand all sit on top. The aircraft is priced by the flight hour for the entire aircraft rather than per passenger, which means a full nine-seat cabin brings the per-person cost below $280 an hour while a solo traveler pays the whole rate.
The Published Range, And Why Nobody Agrees On It

Simple Flying's analysis of private jet charter pricing in 2026 places turboprops, including the Pilatus PC-12 and the Beechcraft King Air 350i at $2,000 to $3,000 per hour, drawing on figures from charter operators BlackJet and Amalfi Jets . That is the most defensible number available, and it sits roughly in the middle of what the wider market publishes.

The spread around it is considerable. Charter brokers quoting the PC-12 online put the figure anywhere between $1,000 and $3,500 per hour depending on which page you read, and some publish multiple conflicting ranges across their own site. A prospective customer searching the aircraft will find figures that differ by a factor of three for what is nominally the same product, which says more about how the charter market advertises itself than about what the aircraft costs.

The variation is not purely marketing. An hourly rate for a charter aircraft is a quoted starting point rather than a fixed price, and the figure an operator publishes reflects its own cost base. Aircraft age matters. Base location matters, because an aircraft positioned near the customer flies fewer empty miles to reach them. Cabin configuration, operator overhead, and seasonal demand all feed in. Simple Flying notes that taxes, fuel surcharges, positioning costs, airport fees, and seasonal demand can all dramatically alter the final invoice, which means the hourly rate describes one input into a quote rather than the quote itself.

Private charter is priced by the flight hour for the aircraft rather than per passenger. That structure defines the economics of the category. A PC-12 costs the same whether one person flies or the cabin is full, which means the per-person figure falls as passengers are added and the solo traveler pays the entire rate alone.

Simple Flying makes that point directly, noting that passenger count is what actually determines value rather than the headline hourly figure. Two people on a turboprop at $2,500 an hour are each effectively paying $1,250. The same aircraft carrying eight brings that below $320. Nothing about the aircraft or the flight changes. Only the division does. That is the calculation behind most group charter bookings, where a full cabin can bring the per-person cost within range of a refundable business class fare.

Fuel is a smaller component than most people assume. AOPA recorded the PC-12 NGX burning 414 to 416 pounds per hour at maximum continuous power at 27,000 feet, which works out to roughly 62 gallons an hour. Against an hourly charter rate of $2,500, fuel accounts for a few hundred dollars at most. The balance covers the operator's cost base spread across the hours it expects to fly, including aircraft ownership or financing , maintenance reserves, insurance, crew salaries and training. That is why two operators quoting the same aircraft type arrive at different numbers. The hourly rate is where a business model becomes a price, and the businesses behind identical aircraft are not identical.

The advertised hourly rate is one line on an invoice that usually contains several. Simple Flying lists taxes, fuel surcharges, positioning costs, airport fees, and seasonal demand as factors that can dramatically alter the final figure, and any of them can move a quote by thousands of dollars on a short trip.

Positioning is the one that catches people out. Charter aircraft are based somewhere, and if that somewhere is not the customer's departure airport, the aircraft has to fly empty to reach them and frequently empty to return afterward. Those ferry legs are billable. A two-hour trip on an aircraft based two hours away can be charged as six hours of flying, which triples the cost of the mission without the customer spending any longer in the air. It is also why empty-leg pricing exists, since an operator repositioning an aircraft anyway would rather sell those hours cheaply than fly them for nothing, and it is why basing matters more to a charter quote than most customers expect.

The remaining items accumulate. Landing fees, ramp and handling charges, overnight parking, catering beyond basic provisions, and crew expenses if the trip requires an overnight stay all appear separately. Peak periods carry premiums, with holiday weekends, major sporting events and ski season pushing rates above published figures in the markets concerned. A PC-12 quoted at $2,500 per hour on a weekday in March is not the same aircraft quoted at the same rate on a Friday before Thanksgiving, which is why the hourly figure is best treated as the starting point of a conversation rather than the answer to one.

Simple Flying 's category breakdown places turboprops, including the PC-12 and King Air 350i, at $2,000 to $3,000 per hour, carrying six to nine passengers on missions up to roughly 1,500 miles (2,400 km). That is the entry point to private charter on a crewed aircraft of meaningful size, and the only category where the hourly figure starts with a two.
body_zh: 布兰登从小就对航空充满热情。他参与了飞行模拟器和 VATSIM 社区，这激发了他对航空的兴趣，并最终使他获得了私人飞行员执照。工作之余，他继续增加飞行时间、探索新机场并继续参与航空界。

根据 Simple Flying 根据 BlackJet 和 Amalfi Jets 的数据对私人包机定价进行的分析，到 2026 年包租一架皮拉图斯 PC-12 的成本约为每小时 2,000 至 3,000 美元。这使该飞机与 Beechcraft King Air 350i 一起属于涡轮螺旋桨飞机类别，可搭载 6 至 9 名乘客，执行航程约 1,500 英里（2,400 公里）的任务。这是包租这种尺寸的载人飞机最便宜的方式。

小时费率也是私人航空中最不可靠的数字。包机经纪人公布的 PC-12 数据为每小时 1,000 美元到 3,500 美元之间，之所以存在差距，是因为该费率只是一个起点，而不是一个价格。将飞机带到出发机场的定位航班是收费的，这会使短途旅行的成本增加三倍。税收、燃油附加费、着陆费、船员过夜费用和季节性需求都是最重要的。该飞机按整架飞机的飞行小时而不是每位乘客定价，这意味着九座客舱的每人成本低于每小时 280 美元，而单人旅客则需支付全部费用。
已发布的范围以及为什么没有人同意
Simple Flying 根据包机运营商 BlackJet 和 Amalfi Jets 的数据，对 2026 年私人飞机包机定价进行了分析，将包括皮拉图斯 PC-12 和 Beechcraft King Air 350i 在内的涡轮螺旋桨飞机定价为每小时 2,000 至 3,000 美元。这是最有说服力的数字，它大致位于更广泛市场公布的数字的中间。
其周围的传播范围相当大。包机经纪人在网上引用 PC-12 的数据，根据您阅读的页面，将这个数字定在每小时 1,000 美元到 3,500 美元之间，有些经纪人在自己的网站上发布了多个相互冲突的范围。搜索飞机的潜在客户会发现名义上相同的产品的数字相差三倍，这更多地说明了包机市场如何宣传自己，而不是飞机的成本。

这种变化并不纯粹是营销。包机的每小时费率是一个报价起点，而不是固定价格，运营商公布的数字反映了其自身的成本基础。飞机机龄很重要。基地位置很重要，因为位于客户附近的飞机到达客户的空飞行里程更少。客舱配置、运营商管理费用和季节性需求都会影响到。Simple Flying 指出，税费、燃油附加费、定位成本、机场费用和季节性需求都会极大地改变最终发票，这意味着每小时费率描述的是报价中的一项输入，而不是报价本身。
私人包机按飞机的飞行小时而非每位乘客定价。该结构定义了该类别的经济学。无论是单人飞行还是客舱满员，PC-12 的费用都是相同的，这意味着随着乘客的增加，每人的费用会下降，并且单人旅客需要单独支付全部费用。
Simple Flying 直接指出了这一点，并指出乘客数量才是真正决定价值的因素，而不是每小时的整体数据。乘坐涡轮螺旋桨飞机的两个人，每小时 2,500 美元，实际上每人支付 1,250 美元。搭载 8 架飞机的同一架飞机的价格低于 320 美元。飞机或航班没有任何变化。只有部门可以。这就是大多数团体包机预订背后的计算原理，其中一个完整的客舱可以使每人费用处于可退款商务舱票价的范围内。

燃料的成分比大多数人想象的要小。 AOPA 记录显示，PC-12 NGX 在 27,000 英尺高度以最大连续功率每小时燃烧 414 至 416 磅，相当于每小时约 62 加仑。每小时租费为 2,500 美元，燃油最多也就几百美元。余额涵盖运营商预计飞行时间内的成本基础，包括飞机所有权或融资、维护储备金、保险、机组人员工资和培训。这就是为什么两个运营商引用相同机型时得出的数字不同。小时费率是商业模式成为价格的地方，而同一架飞机背后的业务并不相同。
广告中的每小时费率是发票上的一行，通常包含几行。 Simple Flying 将税费、燃油附加费、定位成本、机场费用和季节性需求列为可能极大改变最终数字的因素，其中任何一个因素都可能使短途旅行的报价上涨数千美元。

定位是吸引人们的因素。包机的基地是某个地方，如果该地方不是客户的出发机场，则飞机必须空飞才能到达目的地，并且通常会空飞然后返回。那些渡轮腿是收费的。乘坐两小时外的飞机进行两小时的旅行可以按六个小时的飞行来收费，这使得任务成本增加了三倍，而无需客户在空中停留更长的时间。这也是空航定价存在的原因，因为无论如何重新定位飞机的运营商宁愿便宜地出售这些时间，也不愿免费飞行，这就是为什么基地对包机报价的影响比大多数客户预期的更重要。
剩余的物品会累积。着陆费、坡道费和装卸费、过夜停车费、超出基本规定的餐饮以及旅行需要过夜的船员费用均单独显示。高峰期会带来溢价，假期周末、重大体育赛事和滑雪季节都会导致价格高于相关市场公布的数据。一架 PC-12 在 3 月份工作日的报价为 2,500 美元/小时，与感恩节前的周五以相同价格报价的飞机不同，这就是为什么每小时的数字最好被视为对话的起点，而不是答案。
Simple Flying 的类别细分将涡轮螺旋桨飞机（包括 PC-12 和 King Air 350i）的价格定为每小时 2,000 至 3,000 美元，可搭载 6 至 9 名乘客执行飞行约 1,500 英里（2,400 公里）的任务。这是乘坐具有有意义尺寸的载人飞机的私人包机的切入点，也是唯一每小时数字以 2 开头的类别。

title_en: Southwest Airlines Auctioning Off Old Oakland Baggage Tugs For $750
title_zh: 西南航空以 750 美元拍卖旧奥克兰行李拖车
summary: The move is attracting attention from aviation enthusiasts and bargain hunters.
summary_zh: 此举吸引了航空爱好者和讨价还价者的关注。
body_en: Experienced ICAO English Language Proficiency Instructor for pilots and ATCOs and conference interpreter who is passionate about facilitating effective communication within aviation-related businesses. Possess a deep understanding of the aviation industry, including aviation regulations, terminology, and industry-specific communication protocols. Has been working at numerous airshows across Europe since 2014. Being an ultralight pilot in her free time, she also promotes safety and efficiency in aviation operations.

Southwest Airlines is auctioning off several electric baggage tugs previously used at Oakland San Francisco Bay Airport (OAK) in California, with starting bids as low as $750 per vehicle. The used ground support equipment (GSE), dating back to 2008, has attracted online attention after its unusual auction listing was shared on Reddit . The sale gives aviation enthusiasts and potential buyers a chance to own a piece of airport equipment for far less than a conventional road vehicle.

The vehicles were originally designed to transport luggage and other equipment around airport aprons. While they may look like oversized utility carts, these specialized machines play an important role in airlines' daily operations, connecting aircraft with baggage-handling facilities and terminals. Their retirement from Oakland also highlights how airlines and airports periodically dispose of surplus equipment, creating opportunities for buyers outside the aviation industry.
Southwest's Former Oakland Baggage Tugs Go Up For Auction

According to PEOPLE , Southwest is offering several of its former baggage tugs through an online auction hosted on GovDeals. The vehicles were previously operated at Oakland San Francisco Bay Airport and are listed as 2008 Charlatte T137 electric baggage tugs. Each has a starting bid of $750, making them a relatively inexpensive proposition for anyone interested in acquiring unusual industrial machinery.

These vehicles are slightly larger than ordinary golf carts. Each tug measures approximately 10 feet, 5 inches (3.18 meters) long, four feet, four inches (1.32 meters) wide, and four feet (1.22 meters) tall. According to Charlatte America , the manufacturer, the T137 is a self-propelled, battery-powered electric tow tractor designed for airport ramp and industrial material-handling operations. Rather than carrying passengers, it is designed to move equipment and baggage trailers around airport facilities.

Importantly, the $750 figure represents the starting bid, so the final price can be higher. Buyers must also arrange and pay for collection of their successful purchases, and GovDeals requires winning bidders to schedule appointments to remove the equipment themselves. Consequently, prospective buyers must consider transportation, battery condition, maintenance requirements, and replacement-part availability.
Southwest also told Simple Flying that it periodically sells surplus equipment as part of its normal management of equipment and assets.

The auction quickly attracted attention beyond the aviation community after a listing was shared in the Reddit community. The original poster joked about finding someone willing to buy one of the vehicles, prompting a lively discussion about possible alternative uses. Some commenters suggested using the tugs as neighborhood transport, while others imagined turning them into parade floats or even organizing an amateur racing competition.

One particularly practical suggestion was to use an airport tug to move agricultural equipment around a farm. Others pointed out that electric baggage tractors could potentially serve as unconventional utility vehicles for people with large properties. However, their airport-specific design means prospective owners would need to consider charging requirements, mechanical condition, operating limitations, and whether the vehicles could legally be used on public roads.

The Charlatte T137 illustrates the specialized nature of airport ground equipment. Baggage tugs are essential to ramp operations, moving multiple luggage trailers between aircraft and baggage handling areas. Their compact design lets them maneuver around crowded aprons, while electric propulsion offers a cleaner alternative to conventional diesel-powered ground support vehicles. For airlines, maintaining a fleet of reliable tugs is essential to keeping aircraft turnaround operations running smoothly .
Airlines Regularly Auction Surplus Aviation Equipment

The Oakland baggage tug sale is not an isolated example of airlines disposing of their surplus ground support equipment. In September 2024, Southwest organized a much larger auction through Starman Bros. Auctions, featuring approximately 119 pieces of equipment located at 31 airports across the US . The inventory included 11 baggage tugs, six pushback tractors, nine ground power units, belt loaders, passenger stairs, heater carts, provisioning trucks, and six forklifts. The inventory also included several ordinary utility vehicles, golf carts, and workshop equipment.

Airports and airlines also periodically dispose of other items they no longer need, including old aircraft seats, cabin furniture, office equipment, and miscellaneous airport property. Even lost-and-found departments can generate unusual auction opportunities. A GovDeals listing illustrates this category, offering a collection of purses and bags classified as unclaimed lost-and-found luggage, sold without their contents and without guarantees about their condition or authenticity.

These sales can attract buyers interested in second-hand equipment, collectors, resellers, and people looking for unusual bargains . As explored by The Guardian , unclaimed luggage auctions have also become a popular curiosity, with buyers sometimes discovering valuable or unexpected belongings inside abandoned suitcases. Whether it is an electric baggage tug, an aircraft cabin seat, or an unclaimed suitcase, the aviation industry occasionally offers the public an unusual opportunity to acquire items that would otherwise remain within airport operations.
body_zh: 经验丰富的国际民航组织飞行员和空中交通管制员英语语言能力讲师以及会议口译员，热衷于促进航空相关业务中的有效沟通。对航空业有深入的了解，包括航空法规、术语和行业特定的通信协议。自 2014 年以来，她一直在欧洲各地的众多航展上工作。作为一名超轻型飞行员，她在业余时间还致力于提高航空运营的安全性和效率。
西南航空正在拍卖以前在加利福尼亚州奥克兰旧金山湾机场 (OAK) 使用的几辆电动行李拖车，起拍价低至每辆车 750 美元。这台二手地面支持设备 (GSE) 的历史可以追溯到 2008 年，在 Reddit 上分享其不同寻常的拍卖清单后，引起了网上的关注。此次出售让航空爱好者和潜在买家有机会以远低于传统公路车辆的价格拥有一件机场设备。
这些车辆最初设计用于在机场停机坪周围运输行李和其他设备。虽然它们看起来像超大的多功能推车，但这些专用机器在航空公司的日常运营中发挥着重要作用，将飞机与行李处理设施和航站楼连接起来。他们从奥克兰退役也凸显了航空公司和机场如何定期处理剩余设备，为航空业以外的买家创造机会。
西南航空前奥克兰行李拖船将被拍卖
据《人物》杂志报道，西南航空将通过 GovDeals 举办的在线拍卖出售几辆以前的行李拖车。这些车辆此前曾在奥克兰旧金山湾机场运营，被列为 2008 Charlatte T137 电动行李拖车。每台起拍价为 750 美元，对于有兴趣购买不寻常工业机械的人来说，这是一个相对便宜的提议。
这些车辆比普通高尔夫球车稍大。每艘拖船长约 10 英尺 5 英寸（3.18 米），宽 4 英尺 4 英寸（1.32 米），高 4 英尺（1.22 米）。据制造商 Charlatte America 介绍，T137 是一款自走式电池供电电动牵引车，专为机场坡道和工业物料搬运作业而设计。它不是运载乘客，而是设计用于在机场设施周围移动设备和行李拖车。
重要的是，750 美元这个数字代表起拍价，因此最终价格可能会更高。买家还必须安排并支付成功购买的物品的收集费用，GovDeals 要求中标者安排预约自行拆除设备。因此，潜在买家必须考虑运输、电池状况、维护要求和更换零件的可用性。
西南航空还告诉 Simple Flying，作为设备和资产正常管理的一部分，它会定期出售剩余设备。
在 Reddit 社区分享清单后，这次拍卖很快引起了航空界以外的关注。最初的发帖者开玩笑说找到了愿意购买其中一辆车的人，引发了关于可能的替代用途的热烈讨论。一些评论者建议将拖船用作社区交通工具，而另一些评论者则想象将它们变成游行花车，甚至组织一场业余赛车比赛。
一个特别实用的建议是使用机场拖船在农场周围移动农业设备。其他人指出，电动行李牵引车有可能成为拥有大量房产的人的非传统多功能车辆。然而，其针对机场的设计意味着潜在车主需要考虑充电要求、机械状况、操作限制以及车辆是否可以在公共道路上合法使用。
Charlatte T137 体现了机场地面设备的专业性。行李拖车对于坡道操作至关重要，可在飞机和行李处理区域之间移动多个行李拖车。它们的紧凑设计使它们能够在拥挤的停机坪周围机动，而电力推进则为传统柴油动力地面支援车辆提供了更清洁的替代方案。对于航空公司来说，维持一支可靠的拖船机队对于保持飞机周转作业顺利进行至关重要。
航空公司定期拍卖剩余航空设备

奥克兰行李拖车出售并不是航空公司处置多余地面支持设备的一个孤立例子。 2024 年 9 月，西南航空通过 Starman Bros. Auctions 组织了一场规模更大的拍卖会，拍卖了位于美国 31 个机场的约 119 件设备。库存包括 11 辆行李拖车、6 辆后推式牵引车、9 辆地面动力装置、皮带装载机、乘客楼梯、加热车、供应卡车和 6 辆叉车。库存还包括几辆普通多用途车、高尔夫球车和车间设备。
机场和航空公司还定期处理不再需要的其他物品，包括旧飞机座椅、机舱家具、办公设备和各种机场财产。即使是失物招领部门也能产生不寻常的拍卖机会。 GovDeals 的列表说明了这一类别，提供了一系列钱包和袋子，这些钱包和袋子被归类为无人认领的失物招领行李，出售时不包含任何物品，也不保证其状况或真实性。
这些销售可以吸引对二手设备感兴趣的买家、收藏家、经销商以及寻找不寻常便宜货的人们。据《卫报》报道，无人认领的行李拍卖也已成为一种流行的好奇心，买家有时会在废弃的手提箱内发现有价值或意想不到的物品。无论是电动行李拖车、机舱座椅还是无人认领的手提箱，航空业偶尔都会为公众提供一个不寻常的机会来获取原本留在机场运营中的物品。

title_en: Why This Airline Wants To Replace Its Airbus A350s From 2030
title_zh: 为什么这家航空公司希望从 2030 年起更换其空客 A350
summary: The paradigm shift coming the Malaysia Airlines' the before the end of the decade.
summary_zh: 马来西亚航空公司将在本世纪末发生范式转变。
body_en: Luke Diaz is a freelance military writer with experience with active duty experience in the US Navy as well as defense and industrial engineering. He is a former Naval Flight Officer who performed tactical air control on the carrier-based E-2 Hawkeye.

While commercial airlines normally operate widebody jets for two decades to spread acquisition costs over time, Malaysia Airlines is diverging from industry norms. Kuala Lumpur's administration has launched a formal evaluation to replace its flagship Airbus A350-900 fleet starting in 2030, when the present jets will be about twelve years old.

This early retirement contradicts traditional airline procedures, which call for operators to keep reliable widebodies for as long as possible. Between 2017 and 2018, Malaysia leased six brand-new A350s from Air Lease Corporation for twelve years. Later, JP Lease Products and Services added a seventh aircraft to accommodate its longest flights.

Airline planners prefer to return the keys to the leasing firms as soon as the agreements expire rather than prolonging the leases to keep the aircraft in service beyond the 2030s. Malaysia Airlines can reconsider its seating arrangements, increase its fleet size, and resolve the financial issues associated with its current long-haul system by retiring 12-year-old aircraft on schedule.
Stretched Too Thin: The Trap Of A Seven-Jet Flagship Fleet

Malaysia employs a small sub-fleet of seven A350-900 aircraft for its longest intercontinental flights. Each aircraft is powered by two Rolls-Royce Trent XWB-84 engines that generate 84,200 pounds (38,192 kg/374.5 kN) of thrust and has a maximum takeoff weight of 617,294 pounds (280 metric tons). The airline can fly 8,100 nautical miles (15,000 km) nonstop from Kuala Lumpur to key cities in Europe without stopping to refuel, thanks to the jet's combined power and fuel capacity.

There is no margin for error when operating an international schedule with just seven aircraft. The airline's long-haul capacity drops by more than 14% when even one of the sub-fleet's seven aircraft is grounded. When aviation authorities mandated fuel line checks for the Trent XWB engines, that math became a serious issue. Pulling one A350 into the hangar creates a huge gap in the schedule that the airline finds difficult to fill.

"So, for us, we want to keep growing our fleet, and as you know, we've got a total order of 40 aircraft that will be in by 2030," a Malaysia Airlines representative told Simple Flying. "So that will complete our mid- to semi-long-range fleet, right, by 330 meters, and then we'll now move on to what we do with the 350s. So we're going through an exercise right now to do a selection of the aircraft."
Follow the sky's most interesting moments, live
Holds, diversions and rare aircraft, spotted as they happen. Free, no signup.

Performance is also impacted by the aircraft's interior design. To give passengers more room, Malaysia only installed 286 seats on its A350s, comprising four business suites, 35 business class seats, and 247 economy seats. Malaysia Airlines sells over 40 fewer tickets per flight while paying the same fuel and landing fees, since other airlines can fit about 325 seats on the same aircraft.
Thin Margins, Cabin Comfort & The Race For Factory Slots

Malaysia Aviation Group's bottom line is disproportionately impacted by its A350 widebodies. The company cannot afford to squander money on ineffective overhead after reporting a net profit of RM766 million ($162 million) in 2023, its first successful year in 10. These hard-earned earnings are gradually eroded by the cost of separate pilot simulator training, extra engines, and specialist maintenance equipment for just seven aircraft.

Passenger comfort is also a major factor in the replacement search, especially cabin pressure. Because the Airbus A350 is built out of carbon-fiber composites, it can safely pressurize the cabin to feel like 6,000 feet (1,829 meters) while cruising at 43,000 feet (13,106 meters), whereas older metal-bodied designs like the A330neo sit closer to 8,000 feet (2,438 meters) to prevent metal fatigue. That lower cabin altitude reduces jet lag and dry air, so downgrading passengers to a less comfortable plane would hurt Malaysia Airlines against fierce regional competitors like Singapore Airlines.

Getting new airplanes by 2030 requires overcoming enormous production backlogs at both main aircraft manufacturers. Airbus has already sold out most of its widebody production slots through the end of the decade due to part and engine delays, but Boeing is grappling with tight federal safety oversight and supply chain bottlenecks that have hampered twin-aisle deliveries. If Malaysia Airlines takes too long to place an order, it may miss the 2030 deadline and be forced to renew its current A350 leases at significantly higher market prices.
Caught In The Middle: Solving The A330neo Range Gap

The carrier's investment in 40 A330-900neos is directly responsible for the urgency of the present-day fleet reorganization. The 297-seat aircraft is powered by Trent 7000 engines that generate 72,834 pounds (33,037 kg) of power (324 kN) and a takeoff weight of 553,360 pounds (251 metric tons). Winter headwinds reduce its range to 7,200 nautical miles (13,334 km), but nonstop flights to London are still feasible.

This performance disparity places the seven A350-900s in a unique operational scenario. When an ultra-long-range jet designed for fourteen-hour oceanic crossings is flown on medium-haul trips to Australia, money is lost in landing fees and structural bulk. However, because the A330-900neo cannot consistently reach Europe, the airline must rely on a limited, expensive sub-fleet until current leases expire.

Malaysia intends to remove network friction by implementing a single platform capable of flying nonstop to Europe while carrying a high seat count to Australia. Offering identical cabin products along the Kangaroo Route creates a unified passenger experience. Balancing long-haul structural capability with low regional operating costs remains the carrier's core engineering challenge.

body_zh: 卢克·迪亚兹 (Luke Diaz) 是一位自由军事作家，拥有在美国海军以及国防和工业工程领域服役的现役经验。他是一名前海军飞行军官，曾在舰载 E-2 鹰眼上执行战术空中控制。
虽然商业航空公司通常会运营宽体喷气式飞机二十年，以随着时间的推移分摊购置成本，但马来西亚航空公司却偏离了行业规范。吉隆坡政府已启动一项正式评估，以从 2030 年开始更换其旗舰空客 A350-900 机队，届时现有飞机的机龄约为 12 年。
这种提前退役与传统的航空公司程序相矛盾，传统的航空公司程序要求运营商尽可能长时间地保留可靠的宽体飞机。 2017年至2018年间，马来西亚向航空租赁公司租赁了六架全新A350飞机，为期十二年。后来，JP Lease Products and Services 添加了第七架飞机，以适应其最长的航班。
航空公司规划者更愿意在协议到期后立即将钥匙归还给租赁公司，而不是延长租约以让飞机在 2030 年代之后继续服役。马来西亚航空可以重新考虑其座位安排、扩大机队规模，并通过按计划退役 12 年机龄的飞机来解决与当前长途系统相关的财务问题。
捉襟见肘：七架喷气式旗舰机队的陷阱

马来西亚雇佣了一支由七架 A350-900 飞机组成的小型机队来执行其最长的洲际航班。每架飞机均由两台劳斯莱斯遄达 XWB-84 发动机提供动力，可产生 84,200 磅（38,192 千克/374.5 kN）的推力，最大起飞重量为 617,294 磅（280 公吨）。得益于该飞机的综合动力和燃油容量，该航空公司可以从吉隆坡直飞 8,100 海里（15,000 公里），直飞欧洲主要城市，无需停下来加油。
在只有七架飞机的国际航班时刻表上，不允许出现任何错误。即使该支队的 7 架飞机中只有一架停飞，该航空公司的长途运力也会下降 14% 以上。当航空当局强制要求对遄达 XWB 发动机进行燃油管路检查时，数学问题就成了一个严重的问题。将一架 A350 拉入机库会造成航班时刻表上的巨大空白，而该航空公司发现很难填补这一空白。
“因此，对我们来说，我们希望继续扩大我们的机队规模，正如你所知，我们总共收到了 40 架飞机的订单，预计到 2030 年交付，”马来西亚航空公司的一位代表告诉 Simple Flying。 “这将完成我们的中远程机队，对吧，330 米，然后我们现在将继续我们对 350 的工作。所以我们现在正在进行演习来选择飞机。”
追踪天空最有趣的时刻，直播
等待、改航和稀有飞机，一目了然。免费，无需注册。
性能还受到飞机内部设计的影响。为了给乘客更多的空间，马来西亚只在A350飞机上安装了286个座位，其中包括四个商务套房、35个商务舱座位和247个经济舱座位。在支付相同的燃油和着陆费的情况下，马来西亚航空每趟航班的销售量减少了 40 多张机票，因为其他航空公司的同一架飞机可容纳约 325 个座位​​。
微薄的利润、客舱舒适度以及工厂舱位的争夺
马来西亚航空集团的利润受到 A350 宽体飞机的影响尤为严重。该公司在 2023 年报告了 7.66 亿令吉（1.62 亿美元）的净利润，这是该公司 10 年来的第一个成功年份，因此无法承受将资金浪费在无效的管理费用上。这些来之不易的收入逐渐被单独的飞行员模拟器培训、额外的发动机和仅七架飞机的专业维护设备的成本所侵蚀。

乘客舒适度也是寻找替代品的主要因素，尤其是机舱压力。由于空客 A350 采用碳纤维复合材料制成，因此在 43,000 英尺（13,106 米）巡航时，它可以安全地将机舱加压至 6,000 英尺（1,829 米），而 A330neo 等较旧的金属机身设计则位于更接近 8,000 英尺（2,438 米）的高度，以防止金属疲劳。较低的机舱高度可以减少时差和干燥的空气，因此将乘客降级到不太舒适的飞机将损害马来西亚航空与新加坡航空等激烈的区域竞争对手的竞争。
要到 2030 年获得新飞机，两家主要飞机制造商都需要克服巨大的生产积压问题。由于零件和发动机的延误，空中客车公司在本世纪末已经售出了大部分宽体机生产位置，但波音公司正在努力应对严格的联邦安全监督和供应链瓶颈，这些瓶颈阻碍了双通道交付。如果马航下订单的时间太长，它可能会错过 2030 年的最后期限，并被迫以高得多的市场价格续签目前的 A350 租赁合同。
夹在中间：解决 A330neo 航程差距
该航空公司对 40 架 A330-900neos 的投资直接导致了当前机队重组的紧迫性。这架 297 座飞机由 Trent 7000 发动机提供动力，可产生 72,834 磅（33,037 公斤）功率（324 kN），起飞重量为 553,360 磅（251 公吨）。冬季逆风将其航程缩减至 7,200 海里（13,334 公里），但直飞伦敦的航班仍然可行。
这种性能差异使七架 A350-900 处于独特的运行场景中。当一架专为十四小时跨越海洋而设计的超远程喷气式飞机在飞往澳大利亚的中程旅行中飞行时，着陆费和结构体积会造成金钱损失。然而，由于 A330-900neo 无法持续​​到达欧洲，因此该航空公司必须依赖有限且昂贵的子机队，直到当前租约到期。
马来西亚打算通过实施一个单一平台来消除网络摩擦，该平台能够直飞欧洲，同时承载大量座位飞往澳大利亚。袋鼠航线沿线提供相同的客舱产品，打造统一的乘客体验。平衡远程结构能力与低区域运营成本仍然是该航空公司面临的核心工程挑战。

The UK’s Insolvency and Companies Court ordered the compulsory liquidation of Global Airlines Ltd on 4 November 2026, following a creditor petition filed in May. The winding-up notice was published in The Gazette on 12 November.

Founded by James Asquith in 2021, the British start-up planned to build a transatlantic network around the Airbus A380. It never obtained its own air operator certificate. Its only passenger services were a series of charter flights linking Glasgow and Manchester with New York in May 2025, operated by Hi Fly Malta under the Global Airlines brand.
The venture’s sole A380, 9H-GLOBL , has been in storage at Tarbes in south-west France since July 2025. Its fate remains unclear.
Companies House also records a separate application to strike Global Airlines Aircraft Ltd off the register. The court’s winding-up order concerns Global Airlines Ltd .

World of Hyatt Business Card annual fee : $199

World of Hyatt Business Card cons include the lack of an anniversary free night award, lack of lounge access, and lack of meaningful credits (beyond $100) to help offset the annual fee

World of Hyatt Business Card bonus of 70K points
The World of Hyatt Business Card is offering an elevated welcome bonus where you can earn 70,000 World of Hyatt bonus points after spending $7,000 within the first three months.

Based on my latest miles & points valuations , I consider World of Hyatt points to be worth 1.4 cents each. That means I value the 70,000 points at $980, making this a solid bonus. This is a better bonus than what’s typically offered on the personal World of Hyatt Credit Card, making it a compelling reason to pick up the business card.

body_en: SpaceX catches Starship after orbital flight but loses booster - Aviation24.be
Home Space SpaceX SpaceX catches Starship after orbital flight but loses booster

SpaceX caught its Starship spacecraft with the launch tower’s mechanical arms at Starbase in Texas on Saturday, 14 November 2026, marking the first time the upper stage had been recovered this way after returning from orbit. The catch came about 22 hours after lift-off. The Super Heavy booster was lost during its return, preventing SpaceX from recovering both stages on the same flight.

Starship completed 14 orbits at an altitude of about 265 km and deployed 26 Starlink satellites. It was the 15th full-scale Starship flight since testing began in 2023 and the second to reach orbit. SpaceX said the spacecraft’s heat shield appeared to have performed as expected.

SpaceX said the booster’s engines shut down too early during its return. Its guidance system detected that it was out of position, and the booster diverted away from the landing site before its flight termination system activated over the Gulf of Mexico. Engineers are investigating why the engines shut down prematurely.

The catch marks a step towards SpaceX’s goal of recovering and rapidly reusing both stages. NASA welcomed the result as it prepares to test lunar lander docking in Earth orbit on Artemis III. The agency is targeting 2028 at the earliest for Artemis IV, its first planned crewed lunar landing since Apollo.

首页 太空 SpaceX SpaceX 在轨道飞行后捕获了 Starship，但失去了助推器
2026 年 11 月 14 日星期六，SpaceX 在德克萨斯州的 Starbase 用发射塔的机械臂捕获了其 Starship 飞船，这标志着上级在从轨道返回后首次以这种方式回收。升空后约 22 小时，捕获物来了。超重型助推器在返回过程中丢失，导致 SpaceX 无法在同一次飞行中恢复两个阶段。
星舰在高度约265公里的地方完成了14次轨道飞行，部署了26颗星链卫星。这是自 2023 年测试开始以来第 15 次全尺寸星舰飞行，也是第二次进入轨道。 SpaceX 表示，飞船的隔热罩似乎表现符合预期。
SpaceX 表示，助推器的发动机在返回过程中过早关闭。它的制导系统检测到它偏离了位置，助推器在其飞行终止系统在墨西哥湾上空启动之前偏离了着陆点。工程师正在调查发动机过早关闭的原因。
这次捕获标志着 SpaceX 朝着回收和快速重复利用两个阶段的目标迈出了一步。美国宇航局对这一结果表示欢迎，因为它准备在阿耳忒弥斯三号上测试月球着陆器在地球轨道上的对接。该机构的目标是最早在 2028 年进行阿耳忒弥斯四号任务，这是自阿波罗计划以来首次计划载人登月。

title_en: US ground stop exposes risks in FAA network upgrades
title_zh: 美国地面站暴露联邦航空局网络升级风险
summary: The nationwide US ground stop on 13 November 2026 began during routine work on the Federal Aviation Administration’s telecommunications network. The FAA says a surge in connection attempts disrupted radio communications and radar feeds at facilities nationwide
summary_zh: 2026 年 11 月 13 日，美国联邦航空管理局电信网络例行工作期间开始在美国全国范围内进行地面停靠。 F
body_en: US ground stop exposes risks in FAA network upgrades - Aviation24.be
Home Organisations Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) US ground stop exposes risks in FAA network upgrades

The nationwide US ground stop on 13 November 2026 began during routine work on the Federal Aviation Administration’s telecommunications network. The FAA says a surge in connection attempts disrupted radio communications and radar feeds at facilities nationwide. Transport Secretary Sean Duffy blamed ageing infrastructure, a problem federal auditors have documented for years. The FAA’s preliminary account points to a more specific question: why did a router replacement at a remote site cause disruption on a national scale?

FAA contractor L3Harris was installing a router at a radio communications site in El Dorado, Arkansas, as part of work to replace copper lines with fibre. The FAA identified that site and a radar site in Amarillo, Texas, as possible sources of a surge of roughly 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds. L3Harris isolated both sites, after which the network stabilised. The FAA also disabled the same function on about 60 similar routers as a precaution.

The FAA’s 15 November update said 17 of its 22 en-route control centres experienced instability, along with several terminal approach control facilities. Some radio frequencies and radar feeds remained available, allowing controllers to communicate with and track aircraft already in the air. Departures resumed at 20:15 EST , and disruption continued into Sunday. The FAA counted approximately 12,462 cancellations on Friday, a total that includes flights cancelled for reasons other than the ground stop.

The case for replacing ageing equipment is well documented. In 2024, the US Government Accountability Office reported that the FAA had classified 51 of 138 air traffic control systems as unsustainable and another 54 as potentially unsustainable. A September 2026 audit identified a separate problem with the upgrade itself: the FAA had 11,389 individual project schedules for the first phase and no integrated master schedule. The auditors found that installations at the same sites were generally scheduled without coordinating the work to minimise disruption to controllers. An FAA-commissioned safety review had already warned in 2023 about keeping existing systems available during the transition.

Duffy initially blamed Congress for failing to fund a replacement system. Congress had already appropriated $12.5 billion in July 2025 for modernisation, and on the day of the outage, the administration sought another $30.1 billion for airports and air traffic control . The September audit found that the FAA still lacked both a reliable estimate of the programme’s full costs and a coordinated schedule for carrying out its first phase.

The FAA and L3Harris are still investigating why the surge began. Duffy raised equipment failure and installation error as possibilities, and the FAA says it has found no indication of a cyberattack. The agency also says it will review when it carries out such work. Its public account has yet to explain what safeguards were in place to contain a fault at either site, or how much capacity backup systems could provide once the disruption spread. Those findings will help establish how much of the failure stemmed from ageing equipment and how much from the way the upgrade was designed and carried out.
Sources: Federal Aviation Administration , U.S. GAO , reuters.com

首页 组织 美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 美国地面停靠站暴露了 FAA 网络升级的风险
2026 年 11 月 13 日，美国联邦航空管理局电信网络例行工作期间开始在美国全国范围内进行地面停靠。美国联邦航空局表示，连接尝试的激增扰乱了全国设施的无线电通信和雷达信号。交通部长肖恩·达菲将此归咎于基础设施老化，这是联邦审计员多年来记录的一个问题。美国联邦航空局的初步报告指出了一个更具体的问题：为什么在远程站点更换路由器会导致全国范围内的中断？
FAA 承包商 L3Harris 正在阿肯色州埃尔多拉多的一个无线电通信站点安装路由器，作为用光纤替代铜线的工作的一部分。 FAA 确定该站点和德克萨斯州阿马里洛的一个雷达站点可能是每四到五秒大约 1,000 次连接尝试激增的来源。 L3Harris 隔离了两个站点，之后网络稳定下来。作为预防措施，FAA 还禁用了大约 60 个类似路由器上的相同功能。
美国联邦航空局 11 月 15 日更新称，其 22 个航路控制中心中有 17 个以及多个航站楼进近控制设施出现不稳定。一些无线电频率和雷达信号仍然可用，允许管制员与已经在空中的飞机进行通信和跟踪。美国东部时间 20:15 恢复出发，航班中断一直持续到周日。美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 统计，周五约有 12,462 架航班被取消，其中包括因地面停靠以外的原因取消的航班。

更换老化设备的案例已有充分记录。 2024 年，美国政府问责办公室报告称，美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 将 138 个空中交通管制系统中的 51 个列为不可持续系统，另有 54 个系统列为潜在不可持续系统。 2026 年 9 月的一次审计发现了升级本身的一个单独问题：FAA 有 11,389 个第一阶段的单独项目时间表，没有综合的主时间表。审计人员发现，同一地点的安装通常是在没有协调工作的情况下安排的，以尽量减少对控制器的干扰。美国联邦航空局 (FAA) 委托的安全审查已于 2023 年发出警告，要求在过渡期间保持现有系统的可用性。
达菲最初指责国会未能为更换系统提供资金。国会已于 2025 年 7 月拨款 125 亿美元用于现代化改造，在停电当天，政府又寻求另外 301 亿美元用于机场和空中交通管制。 9 月份的审计发现，美国联邦航空局仍然缺乏对该计划全部成本的可靠估计，也缺乏执行第一阶段的协调时间表。
FAA 和 L3Harris 仍在调查激增的原因。达菲提出了设备故障和安装错误的可能性，美国联邦航空局表示尚未发现网络攻击的迹象。该机构还表示，将在开展此类工作时进行审查。其公共账户尚未解释采取了哪些保护措施来遏制任一站点的故障，或者一旦中断蔓延，备份系统可以提供多少容量。这些发现将有助于确定故障有多少是由于设备老化造成的，有多少是由于升级的设计和实施方式造成的。

title_en: Mispronounced Airline Names: ANA, Etihad, EVA, ITA, JAL, Qatar, Etc.
title_zh: 发音错误的航空公司名称：ANA、Etihad、EVA、ITA、JAL、Qatar 等。
summary: Airline names trip people up because of acronyms versus initialisms and foreign-language origins. Here's how ANA, Etihad, EVA, ITA, JAL, Lufthansa, Qatar, SAS and others are officially pronounced.
summary_zh: 由于首字母缩略词、首字母缩略词和外语来源，航空公司的名称让人感到困惑。以下是全日空 (ANA)、阿提哈德 (Etihad)、长荣 (EVA)、意大利 (ITA)、日航 (JAL)、汉莎 (Lufthansa)、Qa
body_en: Pronouncing airline names can be complicated for a variety of reasons. Often this confusion comes down to acronyms vs. initialisms, with the former being abbreviations that are pronounced as words, and the latter being abbreviations that are pronounced as letters. In other situations, the confusion can come down to the name originating in a foreign language, and deciding how that should be said in English.

With that in mind, I figure it would be fun to cover some of the airline names that people struggle with the most. I wrote a similar post last year, but I want to add a few more airlines, and I’ve also picked up a few tricks based on reader feedback last time.

Let me emphasize that I have no claims of being a language expert. For that matter, there’s often more than one acceptable way to pronounce the name of an airline, and it also depends on whether you’re speaking in English, or in the carrier’s native language. But this is intended to be a general and basic guide based on how carriers choose to market themselves.
With that in mind, let’s cover some of the airlines that tend to cause the most confusion…

Japanese Star Alliance carrier All Nippon Airways has the abbreviation “ANA,” and that’s generally sounded out letter by letter. So you’d call it “A-N-A, and not “anna.” It’s a different story in Japanese, but I’m trying to keep things simple here…
If you want to pronounce Abu Dhabi-based Etihad Airways’ name correctly without overcomplicating things, you’re pretty safe if you go with “e-ti-had,” pronounced as three syllables.

That being said, if you truly want to pronounce it correctly and be a little more authentic to the Arabic pronunciation, go with “it-ti-haad,” strange as it might sound in English. That’s because in Arabic (based on my understanding), the “e” sounds a little more like an “i,” and the “t” sound is also a little different.

Taiwanese Star Alliance carrier EVA Air is supposed to be pronounced as “E-V-A Air.” Personally I think just pronouncing it as “ee-vah” sounds so much nicer, but that’s not the official pronunciation. That being said, lots of people do still refer to the airline as “ee-vah,” so odds are that people will know what you’re talking about if you pronounce it that way. For example, it’s much more common to sound out “EVA” than it is to sound out “ANA.”

Italian national carrier ITA Airways is sounded out “ee-tah,” rather than reading out the letters as “I-T-A.” This is also in part because in Italian, the letter “I” is pronounced as a long “E,” while the “A” in Italian is pronounced as a short “A,” which explains why it’s pronounced this way.

Japanese oneworld carrier Japan Airlines has the abbreviation “JAL,” and generally that’s sounded out as one syllable. So you’d call it “jahl,” rather than “J-A-L.” Now, some people still do call it “J-A-L,” but that’s not the way it’s pronounced in official marketing. It’s interesting to see how ANA and JAL approach this differently. Again, this is specific to English — in Japanese, it would be pronounced “ja-ru,” as I understand it.
Polish Star Alliance carrier LOT Polish Airlines is supposed to be pronounced as “lot.” As long as you don’t pronounce it “l-o-t,” you’re good.

Since I speak German, I’m confused by how people are confused about how to pronounce Lufthansa. It’s just “luft-hansa,” exactly as it’s spelled, no? Then again, I’m similarly confused by people not understanding how to pronounce my last name, so that might just be my bias.

The key things to understand are that you don’t want to go too strong on the “loo” sound at the front, the middle of the word doesn’t have a traditional English “th” sound, and the word doesn’t end in “stansa,” as I’ve sometimes heard.

Qatar Airways is known for being one of the world’s best airlines, but how do you pronounce its name? I suppose this comes down to whether you want to pronounce the carrier’s name in an Arabic-sounding way, or more of an English-sounding way. I’m by no means an expert on Arabic, but generally the airline officially pronounces the carrier’s name in two syllables, as “kah-tahr.”

Some mild deviations from that are fine as well, like depending on where you want to put the emphasis. While “cutter” isn’t the correct way to pronounce it, it does seem to be a common way for Brits to say it. No matter what, avoid the beginning of the word being along the lines of “kwah” or “kyu.”

SkyTeam carrier Scandinavian Airlines is commonly abbreviated as SAS. In Northern Europe (at SAS hubs), you’ll generally hear people refer to the airline as “sass,” saying it all as one syllable. Outside of the region it’s common to hear people sound out the letters, “S-A-S,” but that’s not the official way it’s pronounced.
Portuguese Star Alliance carrier TAP Air Portugal Air is supposed to be pronounced as “tap.” It’s not “t-a-p,” so in that sense, it follows more of the SAS approach than the EVA approach.

It can be hard for the average person to keep track of the names of airlines. While some airline names can be hard to pronounce due to the words originating in foreign languages, in other cases it’s hard to figure out whether a carrier’s abbreviated name is using acronyms or initialisms.

The above are some of the airlines I see people most struggle with, so hopefully that’s a useful rundown of how to go about pronouncing a carrier’s name, based on how they officially present themselves. Of course in many cases there are variants that are widely used, and it’s not the end of the world if you don’t get the pronunciation right.
While we’re on the topic, if you ask me, “OMAAT” should be pronounced “oh-matt.” 😉
body_zh: 由于多种原因，航空公司名称的发音可能会很复杂。这种混淆通常归结为首字母缩略词与缩写词，前者是发音为单词的缩写，后者是发音为字母的缩写。在其他情况下，混乱可能归结为源自外语的名称，以及如何用英语表达该名称。
考虑到这一点，我认为涵盖一些人们最难以理解的航空公司名称会很有趣。我去年写过一篇类似的文章，但我想添加更多航空公司，并且我还根据上次读者的反馈学到了一些技巧。
让我强调一下，我并不声称自己是语言专家。就此而言，通常有不止一种可接受的航空公司名称发音方式，而且这还取决于您是用英语还是航空公司的母语说话。但这是基于运营商如何选择自我营销的一般和基本指南。
考虑到这一点，让我们来介绍一些最容易引起混乱的航空公司……
日本星空联盟航空公司全日空航空公司的缩写为“ANA”，通常是一个字母一个字母地发音。所以你可以称其为“A-N-A”，而不是“anna”。在日语中这是一个不同的故事，但我试图让事情变得简单......
如果您想正确发音总部位于阿布扎比的阿提哈德航空公司的名称，而又不想让事情变得过于复杂，那么如果您使用“e-ti-had”（发音为三个音节），那么您会非常安全。
话虽这么说，如果你真的想正确发音并且更地道一点阿拉伯语发音，请选择“it-ti-haad”，尽管它在英语中听起来可能很奇怪。那是因为在阿拉伯语中（根据我的理解），“e”听起来更像“i”，“t”声音也有点不同。
台湾星空联盟航空公司长荣航空应该发音为“E-V-A Air”。就我个人而言，我认为将其发音为“ee-vah”听起来更好，但这不是官方发音。话虽这么说，很多人仍然将航空公司称为“ee-vah”，所以如果你这样发音，人们很可能会知道你在说什么。例如，发音“EVA”比发音“ANA”更常见。
意大利国家航空公司 ITA Airways 的发音是“ee-tah”，而不是读成“I-T-A”。这也部分是因为在意大利语中，字母“I”发音为长“E”，而意大利语中的“A”发音为短“A”，这解释了为什么它会这样发音。
日本寰宇一家航空公司日本航空 (Japan Airlines) 的缩写为“JAL”，通常发音为一个音节。所以你可以称之为“jahl”，而不是“J-A-L”。现在，有些人仍然称其为“J-A-L”，但这不是官方营销中的发音方式。看看全日空和日航如何以不同的方式处理这个问题很有趣。再说一次，这是英语特有的——按照我的理解，在日语中，它会发音为“ja-ru”。
波兰星空联盟航空公司 LOT 波兰航空公司应该发音为“lot”。只要你不把它读成“l-o-t”，你就可以了。
因为我说德语，所以我对人们对 Lufthansa 发音的困惑感到困惑。这只是“luft-hansa”，正如它的拼写一样，不是吗？话又说回来，我同样对人们不明白如何发音我的姓氏感到困惑，所以这可能只是我的偏见。
需要理解的关键是，你不想在前面的“loo”发音上表现得太强，单词的中间没有传统的英语“th”发音，并且这个单词不会像我有时听到的那样以“stansa”结尾。
卡塔尔航空被誉为世界上最好的航空公司之一，但它的名字如何发音呢？我想这取决于您是否想以阿拉伯语发音或英语发音来发音运营商名称。我绝不是阿拉伯语专家，但通常航空公司将航空公司的名称正式发音为两个音节，即“kah-tahr”。
一些轻微的偏差也很好，比如取决于你想把重点放在哪里。虽然“cutter”不是正确的发音，但它似乎是英国人的常见发音方式。无论如何，避免单词的开头是“kwah”或“kyu”。
天合联盟承运商斯堪的纳维亚航空通常缩写为 SAS。在北欧（在 SAS 枢纽），您通常会听到人们将航空公司称为“sass”，全都用一个音节来表示。在该地区之外，经常听到人们读出字母“S-A-S”，但这不是它的官方发音。
葡萄牙星空联盟航空公司 TAP Air Bulgaria Air 的发音应该是“tap”。它不是“t-a-p”，因此从这个意义上说，它更多地遵循 SAS 方法而不是 EVA 方法。
对于普通人来说，记住航空公司的名称可能很困难。虽然某些航空公司的名称可能由于源自外语的单词而难以发音，但在其他情况下，很难确定航空公司的缩写名称是否使用首字母缩略词或首字母缩写词。
以上是我看到人们最纠结的一些航空公司，所以希望这是一个有用的概述，说明如何根据航空公司的官方形象来发音。当然，在很多情况下，都有广泛使用的变体，如果你发音不正确，也不是世界末日。
当我们谈论这个话题时，如果你问我，“OMAAT”应该发音为“oh-matt”。 😉

title_en: World Of Hyatt Credit Card Review: Why It’s My Go-To Hotel Card
title_zh: 凯悦天地信用卡评论：为什么它是我的首选酒店卡
summary: The World of Hyatt Credit Card pairs a $95 annual fee with a free anniversary night and Discoverist status. Here's why I carry it and spend $15K on it.
summary_zh: 凯悦天地信用卡年费为 95 美元，可享受免费周年纪念日住宿和探索者会员资格。这就是我携带它并花费 15,000 美元购买它的原因
body_en: The World of Hyatt Credit Card is Hyatt’s co-branded Chase personal credit card. The card has a $95 annual fee, and offers strong benefits that can easily offset that , including an anniversary free night award , elite nights toward status , and more. It can even be worth spending money on the card, in order to unlock an additional free night and/or elite status.

This post is my in-depth World of Hyatt Card review. What makes Hyatt’s personal credit card so brilliant is that it’s worth having regardless of whether you want to keep it just for the ongoing perks, or whether you want to spend money on it.
World of Hyatt Credit Card summary & key details
Before I get into my World of Hyatt Credit Card review, let me briefly summarize the key details of the card
World of Hyatt Card welcome offer : Four Category 1-4 free night awards after spending $5,000 within the first three months

World of Hyatt Card rewards : 4x points on Hyatt spending, 2x points on restaurants, airline tickets purchased directly from airlines, fitness clubs and gym memberships, and local transit and commuting, and 1x points on all other purchases
World of Hyatt Card elite status : World of Hyatt Discoverist status just for being a cardmember, plus two elite nights for every $5,000 spent on the card

World of Hyatt Card benefits & free nights : An anniversary free night award valid at a Category 1-4 property, a second Category 1-4 free night award when you spend $15,000 on the card per calendar year
World of Hyatt Card foreign transaction fees : None
Beyond that, here are what I consider to be some of the major pros and cons of the World of Hyatt Credit Card
World of Hyatt Card pros include a good welcome bonus, an anniversary free night award that easily justifies the annual fee, and a good incentive to spend at least $15,000 on the card per year
World of Hyatt Card cons include the lack of automatic high tier elite status, the lack of credits, and the unexciting return on everyday spending
World of Hyatt Credit Card bonus, eligibility, & fees

When we apply for credit cards, some of the most important factors are the welcome bonus, the eligibility rules for getting the card, and the annual fee. How does the World of Hyatt Credit Card do on those fronts? Let’s take a look.
World of Hyatt Card bonus of four free night awards

At the moment, the World of Hyatt Card is offering a limited time welcome bonus where you can earn four free night awards after spending $5,000 within the first three months. Each free night award is valid at a Category 1-4 World of Hyatt property.

World of Hyatt Category 4 properties retail for up to 25,000 points per night, so the absolute maximum value of this offer is 100,000 points. However, I of course wouldn’t value it that highly. That’s because these free night awards expire 12 months after they’re issued, and you also can’t top off these awards to redeem at more expensive properties. So actually maxing out the value of these isn’t easy.

One thing I should mention is that while I don’t love the lack of flexibility of this welcome offer, it’s significantly better than the standard bonus, which tends to be lackluster. Obviously Chase and Hyatt know that this is a card people will get for the long term value, rather than just for the bonus.
For what it’s worth, based on my latest miles & points valuations , I consider World of Hyatt points to be worth 1.4 cents each.

body_en: UPS Boeing 767 and Copa Boeing 737 collide at Miami Intl. Airport - Aviation24.be

A UPS Boeing 767 freighter and a Copa Airlines Boeing 737 collided while taxiing at Miami International Airport on Saturday evening, November 14. Two people were treated for minor injuries following the incident.
The collision occurred at approximately 9:15 p.m. local time at a taxiway intersection at Miami International Airport (MIA).

According to the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), the Copa Airlines Boeing 737 was taxiing towards its gate when its wingtip struck the nose of the UPS Boeing 767, which was taxiing for departure to Bogotá, Colombia.
The aircraft involved were Copa Airlines flight CM427, arriving from Panama City, and UPS flight 358, a Boeing 767 freighter scheduled to operate to Bogotá.
Preliminary information from the FAA indicates that air traffic controllers had instructed the UPS crew to give way to the arriving Copa flight.
Audio from the incident also captured one of the pilots reporting the collision to air traffic control, saying: “Somebody hit us.”
The impact caused visible damage to both aircraft, including damage to the nose section of the UPS 767 and the wingtip of the Copa 737.
Miami-Dade Fire Rescue responded to the incident. Two people were treated at the scene for minor injuries but did not require hospitalisation.

Despite the collision, Miami International Airport remained operational. Ground traffic was redirected to alternative taxiways following the incident, avoiding a major disruption to airport operations.
UPS confirmed that its crew was safe and said it was cooperating with the authorities investigating the incident.
The FAA is investigating the circumstances surrounding the collision, including the taxiing sequence and communications between air traffic control and the aircraft involved.

The incident comes as US airports are dealing with significant operational pressure following the recent nationwide air traffic disruption, although there is currently no indication that the Miami ground collision was related to the wider FAA disruption.

事件中的音频还捕捉到一名飞行员向空中交通管制报告了这次碰撞，并说道：“有人撞到了我们。”
这次撞击对两架飞机都造成了明显的损坏，包括 UPS 767 的机头部分和 Copa 737 的翼尖损坏。
迈阿密戴德消防救援中心对这一事件做出了回应。两人受轻伤，在现场接受治疗，但不需要住院治疗。

UPS 确认其船员安全，并表示正在配合当局调查该事件。
美国联邦航空局正在调查事故相关情况，包括滑行顺序以及空中交通管制与涉事飞机之间的通信。
此次事件发生之际，美国机场在最近全国范围内的空中交通中断后正面临巨大的运营压力，尽管目前没有迹象表明迈阿密地面碰撞事件与美国联邦航空局更广泛的中断有关。

title_en: Yikes: FAA Union Claims Nationwide Ground Stop Was Totally Avoidable
title_zh: 哎呀：美国联邦航空局联盟声称全国范围内的地面停留是完全可以避免的
summary: The FAA technicians' union says no risk assessment was done before a contractor's router work triggered Friday's four-hour nationwide ground stop, while Secretary Duffy's explanation shifted within a day.
summary_zh: 美国联邦航空局技术人员工会表示，在承包商的路由器工作引发周五全国四小时的地面停留之前，没有进行任何风险评估。
body_en: On Friday, we saw a nationwide ground stop that lasted for around four hours, making it the longest ground stop that we’ve seen in the country in over 25 years, since 9/11. This is of course a major screw-up , and it’ll likely take some time before an investigation fully reveals what the root cause of this was.

So far, the response from Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy has been downright pitiful, and that’s the polite way of putting it. Along those lines, the union representing workers at the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is suggesting that this might’ve been completely avoidable, because unlike in the past, no risk assessment was performed prior to the mistake that caused this mess.
Duffy can’t keep story straight, but is desperate to blame

On Friday night, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin held a press conference to update people on the state of the shutdown. The whole thing felt to me like an SNL skit, because Duffy and Mullin couldn’t even keep their narratives straight, and the whole message was so tone deaf.

Rather than thanking the public for their patience, Duffy went on a rant demanding $50 billion from Congress, suggesting it’s their fault that they haven’t given Trump money for the past year. On Friday night, Duffy suggested the following was the reason that our skies shut down

“What happened is that our switches, actually got overloaded with data, and they went down… I shouldn’t say they went down… they started to give us inconsistency with the data from those routers, and because of that, we shut the system down.”
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed old air traffic control systems for the telecommunication issues behind the FAA nationwide ground stop on Friday.
"Our switches, our routers actually got overloaded with data," he said. "They started to give us inconsistency in the data… pic.twitter.com/5iX8mqL7RP

So he suggested that this was because of switches being overloaded due to how outdated the system is, which of course raised lots of questions about what made Friday different than any other day, in terms of the system being overloaded. Not surprisingly, he didn’t have a good answer, because he was just talking out of his you-know-what.
Very good set of questions from Luke Radel for Secretary Duffy and Secretary Mullin. pic.twitter.com/f6tlfDtbJG
Less than 24 hours later, Duffy switched his tune, explaining the situation as follows

In at least one of our remote FAA locations, a contractor was doing routine maintenance to switch telecommunications lines from old copper wire and they were bringing it over to fiber. That contractor that does the work for us is L3Harris. They are our legacy provider, they’ve been working for the FAA for over 20 years.”
“What we are working to determine was whether we had incompetence, meaning was it user error or installer error from L3Harris, or did they install a faulty router.”

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said FAA contractor L3Harris was working at a remote location to switch telecommunication lines from cooper to fiber, which led to the longest nationwide shutdown of flights since the September 11, 2001, attacks https://t.co/6m0coVd6mo pic.twitter.com/5zdZoINAcA

So on Friday, the problem was that the switches got overloaded due to how old the system was, and Duffy used that to essentially make the press conference a $50 billion demand to modernize air traffic control (which I’m all in favor of, for the record, if done correctly, but this doesn’t seem to be the time or place for this). Then on Saturday, it was a mess up by a contractor.
Does anyone remember when press briefings during a period of crisis were about sharing facts, and not just making random stuff up, and sharing theories that suit narratives? Those were the days…
FAA union says there was no oversight for this project

This is way beyond my area of expertise, but I’m sure I’m not alone in wondering how one contractor can make a mistake that just shuts down our entire aviation ecosystem? Shouldn’t there be a little more oversight so that such a major mistake can’t happen?”

This is where it gets interesting. PASS (“Professional Aviation Safety Specialists”) is the union representing 11,000 workers at the FAA. According to the union, historically projects like this would’ve been overseen by FAA employees with a risk assessment and more coordination, but that hasn’t been happening anymore. Here’s the statement

The issue was isolated to two contractor owned and maintained routers that were being updated mid-day. Historically contractors have followed a protocol where FAA employees conduct a risk assessment and coordinate the maintenance of the system or equipment. PASS-represented technicians were not involved in the upgrades that led to the ground stop yesterday.
body_zh: 周五，我们在全国范围内看到了一次持续约四个小时的地面停留，这是自 9/11 以来 25 年来我们在该国看到的最长的地面停留。这当然是一个重大失误，可能需要一些时间才能进行调查才能完全揭示其根本原因。
到目前为止，交通部长肖恩·达菲的反应非常可怜，这是礼貌的表达方式。沿着这些思路，代表美国联邦航空管理局（FAA）工人的工会表示，这可能是完全可以避免的，因为与过去不同的是，在导致这场混乱的错误之前没有进行风险评估。
达菲无法把故事讲清楚，但又极力指责
周五晚上，交通部长肖恩·达菲和国土安全部部长马克韦恩·穆林举行新闻发布会，向人们通报政府关闭的最新情况。整件事对我来说就像是《周六夜现场》的短剧，因为达菲和穆林甚至无法把他们的叙述说清楚，而且整个信息是如此的充耳不闻。
达菲没有感谢公众的耐心，而是咆哮起来，要求国会提供 500 亿美元，并暗示他们过去一年没有给特朗普钱是他们的错。周五晚上，达菲提出以下是我们天空关闭的原因
“所发生的情况是，我们的交换机实际上数据过载，然后它们就宕机了……我不应该说它们宕机了……它们开始让我们与来自路由器的数据不一致，因此，我们关闭了系统。”
交通部长肖恩·达菲 (Sean Duffy) 将周五美国联邦航空局 (FAA) 全国地面站的电信问题归咎于旧的空中交通管制系统。
“我们的交换机、路由器实际上数据过载了，”他说。 “他们开始给我们带来数据不一致的情况...... pic.twitter.com/5iX8mqL7RP
因此，他认为这是因为系统过时导致交换机过载，这当然引发了很多问题，即就系统过载而言，周五与其他任何一天不同的原因是什么。毫不奇怪，他没有一个好的答案，因为他只是在说他的“你知道的”。
卢克·雷德尔向达菲国务卿和穆林国务卿提出了一系列非常好的问题。 pic.twitter.com/f6tlfDtbJG
不到24小时后，达菲改变了态度，解释了情况如下
至少在美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 的一个偏远地点，一名承包商正在进行日常维护，将电信线路从旧铜线切换为光纤。为我们做这项工作的承包商是 L3Harris。他们是我们的传统供应商，他们已经为 FAA 工作了 20 多年。”
“我们正在努力确定我们是否有能力不足，这意味着是 L3Harris 的用户错误或安装程序错误，还是他们安装了有故障的路由器。”
运输部长 Sean Duffy 表示，FAA 承包商 L3Harris 正在偏远地区工作，将电信线路从铜缆切换为光纤，这导致了自 2001 年 9 月 11 日以来最长的全国航班停飞，攻击 https://t.co/6m0coVd6mo pic.twitter.com/5zdZoINAcA
因此，周五的问题是，由于系统太旧，交换机过载了，达菲利用这一点，在新闻发布会上提出了 500 亿美元的空中交通管制现代化要求（郑重声明，如果做得正确的话，我完全赞成这一点，但这似乎不是这样做的时间或地点）。然后到了周六，承包商就把事情搞砸了。
有谁记得危机时期的新闻发布会是关于分享事实，而不是胡编乱造，以及分享适合叙述的理论？那些日子……
美国联邦航空局工会表示对该项目没有监督
这远远超出了我的专业领域，但我确信我并不是唯一一个想知道承包商怎么会犯下导致我们整个航空生态系统关闭的错误的人？难道不应该多一点监督，避免出现这样的重大错误吗？”
这就是有趣的地方。 PASS（“专业航空安全专家”）是代表 FAA 11,000 名员工的工会。据工会称，历史上此类项目将由美国联邦航空局员工进行监督，并进行风险评估和更多协调，但这种情况已经不再发生。这是声明
该问题是由两个承包商拥有和维护的路由器造成的，这些路由器正在中午进行更新。从历史上看，承包商遵循一项协议，由联邦航空局员工进行风险评估并协调系统或设备的维护。 PASS 代表的技术人员没有参与导致昨天停飞的升级工作。
